title: Scaled Dot-Product Attention in NumPy
description: Score a decoder query q against three encoder keys K, normalize with softmax to get attention weights, and compute the weighted sum of values V.
source: draft: agy free model + edit: codex

steps.description: Import `numpy as np` and define `softmax(x)` to exponentiate `x - x.max()` and divide by the sum so the output weights are positive and add to 1.
Set `K` and `V` to the same `3 x 4` matrix of encoder vectors for `['the', 'black', 'cat']`, and define the 4-element decoder query `q = np.array([0.1, 0.2, 2.0, 1.0])`.
Compute scaled dot-product `scores = K @ q / np.sqrt(4)`, convert them into `weights = softmax(scores)`, and print both `weights` and the blended `context vector` (`weights @ V`).

Trace the three attention steps in lines 11-14. `K @ q / np.sqrt(4)` scores `q` against each row of `K`, and `softmax(scores)` turns those scores into weights. `weights @ V` takes that weighted average of the rows of `V`.

steps.question: Which row of `K` has the largest dot product with `q = [0.1, 0.2, 2.0, 1.0]`, and therefore receives the largest softmax weight?
steps.answer: Row 2 (`[0., 0., 1., 1.]`, corresponding to `'cat'`), whose dot product with `q` is `2.0 + 1.0 = 3.0`, giving it the largest attention weight (`0.56`).

steps.description: Line 13 prints the rounded softmax attention weights `[0.22 0.23 0.56]`, placing the highest weight on `'cat'`.
Line 14 multiplies `weights @ V` and prints `context vector: [0.22 0.23 0.56 1.  ]`.
